topic: Greatest E-separation representatives for finite directed mixed graphs: prove unrestricted single-edge transfer, deduce binary-union closure and simultaneous admissible-edge saturation, and recover the canonical greatest representative and compelled edges from finitely many singleton E-separation queries. Preserve arbitrary directed cycles, self-loops, and bidirected confounding; cover SCC-changing directed additions and bidirected additions outside existing SCC rectangles. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Singleton composition and fixed-profile mixed saturation were derived; exhaustive checks through three vertices and sampled five/six-node tests found no union failure. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: unrestricted single-edge transfer. EARLY KILL TEST: exhaust all five-vertex bases with at most five edges and independently confirm any failure. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_esep_dmg_greatest_complete.md

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when inserting one absent directed or bidirected edge into a finite E-separation DMG preserves its independence model, including SCC-merging arrows, self-loops, and first bidirected connections between SCCs.

source_refs.claim: The paper conjectures greatest E-separation representatives for DMGs, verifies them only through four nodes, and proves bidirected saturation only when the endpoint SCCs already share a bidirected edge.
source_refs.author: Georg Manten, Cecilia Casolo, Søren Wengel Mogensen, Niki Kilbertus
source_refs.venue: CLeaR 2025, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 275

source_refs.claim: For μ-separation DMGs, potential-parent and potential-sibling conditions yield single-edge addition lemmas and a greatest Markov-equivalent supergraph.
source_refs.author: Søren Wengel Mogensen, Niels Richard Hansen

open_problems.why_unsolved: Manten et al.'s mixed-graph transfer argument replaces a newly added bidirected edge using directed paths inside its endpoint SCCs and an already existing bidirected edge between those SCCs; that replacement is unavailable for the first bidirected connection. A directed insertion can instead merge SCCs and change which repeated vertices are unblockable in the time-split graph. The corresponding complete addition machinery is known for μ-separation, but its walk-opening rules differ from E-separation, and the literature scan found no resolution of the 2025 E-separation DMG conjecture.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An if-and-only-if single-edge transfer theorem stated from the pre-insertion E-separation profile, with an open-walk replacement proof for every directed, bidirected, and self-loop regime, or a smallest counterexample class identifying the failing regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly motivates asymmetric path-space discovery, isolates partial observation as the unresolved case, and states the relevant DMG conjecture.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: path-space conditional independence is directional -> latent coordinates induce cyclic DMGs -> the directed-graph representative theorem no longer suffices -> unrestricted edge transfer is the missing local mechanism

method_exemplars.technique: Define potential parents and siblings from the independence model, prove that adding each corresponding edge preserves μ-separation by transforming every newly opened walk, and iterate the additions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the analogous single-edge-to-greatest-representative problem for arbitrary cyclic, confounded DMGs; its μ-open-walk splicing argument is the first proof step that must be replaced.

method_exemplars.technique: Give necessary and sufficient legitimacy conditions for a single mark change and prove that equivalent directed MAGs are connected by sequences of such local transformations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest latent-variable precedent for reducing global equivalence to equivalence-preserving one-edge moves, although its ancestral and acyclic restrictions must be removed.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether every finite E-separation equivalence class of directed mixed graphs is closed under binary edge-set union and therefore has a unique greatest member equal to the union of all representatives.

source_refs.claim: A greatest E-separation representative is proved for directed graphs but only conjectured for DMGs, with exhaustive computational support through four vertices.
source_refs.author: Georg Manten, Cecilia Casolo, Søren Wengel Mogensen, Niki Kilbertus
source_refs.venue: CLeaR 2025, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 275

source_refs.claim: Theorem 5.9 constructs a greatest representative for every μ-separation DMG class and shows that intermediate edge-addition graphs remain equivalent.
source_refs.author: Søren Wengel Mogensen, Niels Richard Hansen

source_refs.claim: Exact μ-Markov equivalence is coNP-complete, whereas coarser weak-equivalence classes admit greatest elements and feasible algorithms.
source_refs.author: Søren Wengel Mogensen

open_problems.why_unsolved: A greatest member is stronger than the existence of individually maximal graphs: two edges harmless relative to one base can interact after the first addition changes SCC ancestry or supplies part of an E-open walk. Manten et al. establish restricted additions and report finite four-node evidence, while the μ-separation construction depends on potential-parent and potential-sibling axioms not known to characterize E-separation. The μ-equivalence complexity result also shows that existence of a greatest element need not by itself make equivalence testing efficient.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a theorem that I_E(G)=I_E(H) implies I_E(G∪H)=I_E(G), yielding G_max=⋃{H:I_E(H)=I_E(G)}, or a minimal finite DMG counterexample together with a sharp sufficient regime for union closure.

writing_exemplar.why: Its directed-versus-partially-observed contrast cleanly motivates whether the canonical representative survives bidirected confounding.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: E-separation supports cyclic path-space discovery -> directed equivalence classes have canonical greatest graphs -> marginalization introduces bidirected edges -> decide whether the canonical-object theorem survives for all DMGs

method_exemplars.technique: Construct the canonical graph from all potential-parent and potential-sibling relations and prove every monotone edge-addition chain to it remains Markov equivalent.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its conclusion is precisely union closure and simultaneous saturation for another asymmetric separation model on the same graph class.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode every DAG Markov-equivalence class by a unique essential graph and prove its construction from invariant adjacencies and orientations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the foundational canonical-representative argument against which a greatest E-DMG object should be formulated, while highlighting the new difficulties from cycles and bidirected edges.

open_problems.open_problem: Give a finite singleton-endpoint E-separation oracle characterization that reconstructs the greatest E-equivalent DMG and classifies every directed, bidirected, and loop edge as compelled, optional, or impossible.

source_refs.claim: Left and right composability reduce the full E-separation calculation to singleton endpoint pairs, while the paper's recovery algorithm and greatest-element proof are restricted to fully observed directed graphs.
source_refs.author: Georg Manten, Cecilia Casolo, Søren Wengel Mogensen, Niki Kilbertus
source_refs.venue: CLeaR 2025, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 275

source_refs.claim: The μ-separation directed mixed equivalence graph marks invariant and non-invariant edges and can be computed from the maximal graph using edge-deletion equivalence tests.
source_refs.author: Søren Wengel Mogensen, Niels Richard Hansen

source_refs.claim: Under σ-Markovness and σ-faithfulness, FCI is sound and complete for several causal features in cyclic SCMs with latent confounding.
source_refs.author: Joris M. Mooij, Tom Claassen
source_refs.venue: UAI 2020, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 124

open_problems.why_unsolved: Composability establishes that singleton endpoints determine the full set-valued E-independence model, but it does not identify which finite subfamily witnesses each candidate arrow, spouse edge, or self-loop. The μ-separation equivalence graph identifies compelled edges by deleting edges from an already known greatest graph; for E-separation that greatest graph remains conjectural, and SCC changes obstruct a naïve addition/deletion duality. The scan found sound-complete feature recovery for σ-separation and an equivalence graph for μ-separation, but no E-separation analogue for partially observed DMGs.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Explicit predicates over singleton queries ({i},{j},C)∈I_E and an algorithm with a finite query bound that outputs G_max and an edge-marking graph, with a theorem equating each mark to presence in all, some, or no representatives.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the equivalence-class representative as the learnable object and treats the greatest graph and invariant edges separately.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: latent coordinates make mixed graphs observationally nonunique -> the independence model determines a greatest representative -> invariant edges require a marked equivalence graph -> reconstruct both objects from separation information

method_exemplars.technique: Translate singleton-endpoint separation implications into potential-parent and potential-sibling predicates, construct the maximal DMG, and mark optional edges by one-edge deletion tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This produces exactly the greatest-plus-compelled-edge object sought here, but for μ-separation rather than E-separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply sound and complete orientation rules to convert separating-set information into all arrowheads and tails common to a MAG equivalence class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired E-equivalence graph likewise needs soundness and completeness for every reported invariant endpoint mark.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate a local covariance measure with cross-fitted nuisance learners and prove uniform size and power control for conditional local-independence tests.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a concrete inference layer for the asymmetric singleton oracle consumed by the combinatorial reconstruction.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a statistically consistent recovery procedure for the greatest E-separation DMG under partially observed cyclic SDEs, with simultaneous error control over all singleton queries used for saturation and compelled-edge labeling.

source_refs.claim: The paper gives a proof-of-concept data algorithm only for fully observed directed graphs; the greatest-representative claim remains conjectural under partial observation.
source_refs.author: Georg Manten, Cecilia Casolo, Søren Wengel Mogensen, Niki Kilbertus
source_refs.venue: CLeaR 2025, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 275

source_refs.claim: Cross-fitted local covariance tests provide uniformly controlled level and power for individual conditional local-independence hypotheses.
source_refs.author: Alexander Mangulad Christgau, Lasse Petersen, Niels Richard Hansen

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes weaker faithfulness conditions for local-independence graphs and studies how independence-test errors affect structure-learning procedures.
source_refs.author: Søren Wengel Mogensen
source_refs.venue: AISTATS 2024, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 238

open_problems.why_unsolved: Uniform validity for one local-independence test does not imply uniform graph recovery after many, potentially adaptive conditioning-set tests. The E-separation paper does not supply multiplicity control, beta-min or E-faithfulness margins, or an analysis of how erroneous oracle answers propagate through SCC formation and mixed-edge saturation. Partial observation also requires the greatest combinatorial target to be proved well-defined before its estimator can be analyzed.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An estimator of the E-greatest DMG and its compelled-edge marks, with a high-probability exact-recovery or uniform-consistency theorem under explicit E-faithfulness and nuisance-rate conditions and an accompanying query and sample-complexity bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It connects E-separation to cyclic SDE discovery and clearly separates the proved fully observed algorithm from the latent-variable conjecture.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: SDE mechanisms are naturally cyclic -> time splitting yields asymmetric E-separation queries -> hidden coordinates require a DMG equivalence-class target -> reliable discovery requires uniform recovery of its canonical representative

method_exemplars.technique: Use cross-fitting and a local covariance measure to obtain limit theory and tests with uniformly controlled size and power under modest nuisance rates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed graph estimator is a deterministic functional of many asymmetric process-independence decisions, making this the closest validated testing and limit-theory module.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate Markov and graded faithfulness assumptions to graphical reconstruction and analyze learning procedures under erroneous independence decisions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Recovery of the E-greatest graph needs the same bridge from an oracle characterization to assumptions on the observed stochastic process.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove soundness and completeness of constraint-based orientation under σ-separation for cyclic SCMs with latent confounders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest sound-complete discovery theorem in the cycles-plus-confounding regime, with E-separation replacing σ-separation and a greatest graph replacing a PAG.

literature_map:
Manten, Casolo, Mogensen & Kilbertus (CLeaR 2025, arXiv:2503.09859) is the direct anchor: greatest E-separation DMG representatives are explicitly conjectured and checked only through four nodes.
The same paper proves the directed-graph greatest theorem and data recovery, but its mixed Proposition 3.22 fills only bidirected SCC rectangles already containing a bidirected edge.
Mogensen & Hansen (Annals of Statistics 2020, arXiv:1802.10163) prove the full μ-separation analogue using potential parents, potential siblings, and a directed mixed equivalence graph.
Mogensen (Bernoulli 2025, arXiv:2302.12541) proves exact μ-equivalence coNP-complete and develops tractable weaker equivalences with greatest members.
Mogensen & Hansen (Bernoulli 2022, DOI:10.3150/21-BEJ1446) study correlated-noise process graphs and expose superpolynomial equivalence conditions.
Christgau, Petersen & Hansen (Annals of Statistics 2023, arXiv:2203.13559) provide cross-fitted, uniformly controlled conditional local-independence tests for a singleton-query inference layer.
Mogensen (AISTATS 2024, arXiv:2310.13796) characterizes faithfulness for local-independence graphs and studies distortion from erroneous independence tests.
Forré & Mooij (UAI 2018, arXiv:1807.03024) develop σ-separation discovery for nonlinear cyclic SCMs with latent confounding, but not an E-greatest representative.
Mooij & Claassen (UAI 2020, arXiv:2005.00610) prove FCI sound and complete for several σ-separation causal features with cycles and latent variables.
Richardson (IJAR 1997, DOI:10.1016/S0888-613X(97)00020-0) and Claassen & Mooij (UAI 2023, arXiv:2309.03092) characterize d-separation equivalence for cyclic directed graphs; the latter leaves latent confounding as a frontier.
Richardson & Spirtes (Annals of Statistics 2002, DOI:10.1214/aos/1031689015) establish latent projection and maximal ancestral graphs, whose ancestral restriction excludes the arbitrary cycles required here.
Ali, Richardson & Spirtes (Annals of Statistics 2009, arXiv:0908.3605) give polynomial graphical equivalence conditions for maximal ancestral graphs.
Zhang & Spirtes (UAI 2005, arXiv:1207.1419) reduce directed-MAG equivalence to legitimate single-mark changes; Zhang (Artificial Intelligence 2008, arXiv:1206.5282) gives complete invariant-endpoint rules.
Boeken & Mooij (2024, arXiv:2406.01161) supply dynamic-SCM and time-splitting semantics for cyclic, latently confounded systems; Finkelstein et al. (UAI 2021, arXiv:2107.07087) concern a distinct deletion-based lower-case e-separation notion.
